newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond trade firm, high-yields mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond trade firm, high-yields mixed.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds traded in a higher range with Treasuries on Thursday despite the onset of fresh supply, while high-yields were mixed in the secondary as players focused on the primary there, dealers said.
"The supply has been eaten up pretty quickly and most of the deals that have been priced are trading at or close to original levels," one high-grades trader said.

Campbell Soup Co's $300 million AA3/AA-minus rated 10-year notes were trading in a 36 basis point bid, 35 basis point offer near the close, in line with Wednesday's issue level of 35, one trader said.
Abbey National Plc's $500 million AA3/A-plus perpetual reset note issue tightened to a 76 basis point bid compared with its original issue spread of 78 basis points.

New issuance on Thursday featured $300 million 10-year guaranteed notes from British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc via lead manager Goldman Sachs & Co. The notes were priced as 7.30s to yield 80 basis points over the Treasury curve.

Also on Thursday, Bankers Trust New York added another to the recent string of investment house deals. Through UBS Securities, BT set $150 million A3/A-minus 15-year sub notes as 7.25s to yield 82 basis points over the Treasury 10-year.

UtiliCorp United Inc tapped the market for $100 million Baa3/BBB 10-year senior notes, priced as 6.70s for a spread of 45 basis points over the five year Treasury note. The deal included a put option in the fifth year.
Other secondary trade was quiet by all standards, traders said, with spreads holding firm throughout all sectors.

Prices were lifted early as U.S. Treasuries took heed from government data that suggested the economy slowed in September, players said. Data included a six percent drop in housing starts, a modest 0.2 percent increase in industrial production and a slight decline in capacity utilization.
The uptick was confirmed after the Philadelphia Federal Reserve said its index of regional business activity fell to -5.3 in October from 13.9 in September.

Turning to high-yielders, dealers said new issues were trading in line with original issue spreads or weaker. Kaiser Aluminum and Chemical Corp's $175 million 144A 10-year senior notes, priced on Thursday at 99.50 to yield 440 basis points over Treasuries, were quoted at 99-5/8 at the close.
Dealers noted the calendar was promising heavier supply through November, forcing secondary trade into more work-out type situations.

"The marketplace is trading very sloppy," one high-yield trader said. "The street doesn't want to get long in front of the calendar and the accounts are focusing on the calendar, so you're seeing a gradual slide."
In spot news, debt of Tenet Healthcare Corp and OrNda HealthCorp popped up about one point after news Tenet would acquired OrNda for about $1.8 billion in a tax-free stock transaction, traders said.

Tenet 10.125 percent paper gained a full point on the news to 109-1/2 bid, 110 offer, while the company's 8.625 percent debt rose a 1/2 to trade at 105-1/4 bid, high-yield traders said. OrNda's 11.375 percent paper traded up 3/4 point on the news to 113 bid.

Some telecom paper resumed their fall from lofty levels, traders said, in some spots 20 basis points weaker over the last two sessons. Traders insisted the move is related to technical trade and not the sector's creditworthiness.
Adelphia Communications fell one point to 102-1/4, 103-1/4 market and Lenfest Communications fell 3/4 point. The Lenfest move was said to reflect weakness in TCI Communications.
Marvel Entertainment also fell on Thursday, a trader said.
